title: SRE weekly update 2026-10-10
content:
SRE Weekly Update — 2026-10-10
Owner: Aisha Patel
Summary: Quiet week overall with one customer-impacting incident related to the KV cache service during peak batching; SLOs holding but tail latency creep observed on embeddings endpoints. On-call handoffs continue to be smooth.

1) Incidents and Alerts
- 2026-10-08 14:18 PDT — KV cache degradation (PD-INC-2026-0928)
  - Impact: Elevated error rates and increased latency for model generation endpoints using prefix caching. ~12 minutes of customer-visible errors for a subset of hosted-api traffic.
  - Root cause: A recent rolling deploy of the cache eviction tuning (configs pushed by GH-PR-4821) had an edge case where high-parallel eviction cycles overwhelmed the eviction worker queue under a specific traffic pattern.
  - Mitigation: Rolled back the config change and increased eviction worker parallelism; applied a temporary rate limiter on eviction triggers. Incident closed at 14:30 PDT.
  - Action items: Complete a test harness for eviction storms (owner: Liam Chen, ETA: 2026-10-17); add circuit-breaker to eviction scheduler (owner: Noah Ramirez, ETA: 2026-10-24).

- Minor PagerStorm — several false-positive alerts from health check flapping (flaky synthetic probes) on 2026-10-09 AM. Root cause traced to an overloaded synthetic runner in us-west-2. Mitigation: spun up additional synthetic runners and adjusted probe backoff. Follow-up: Improve probe jitter and add stronger alert suppression for known maintenance windows.

2) SLOs and Metrics
- Availability SLOs: All critical service SLOs met for the week. Hosted API 99.95% availability for platform requests (target 99.9% for paid tiers; note: the 99.9% target applies only to Dedicated customers).
- Latency: Median latency stable; p95/p99 for embeddings endpoints increased by ~18% over baseline during peak hours (11:00–14:00 PDT). Preliminary correlation shows higher cache miss rates and a slight increase in model-side CPU contention.
- Error budget: Small burn observed for the embeddings route; we are within budget but flagged for close monitoring.

3) On-call handoffs and rotations
- This week on-call (primary): Priya Desai; backup: Ethan Brooks. Handoffs documented in the on-call log (linked in Slack thread). No missed handoffs.
- Handoff notes: Priya called out ongoing work to stabilize the eviction scheduler and a planned control-plane deploy on 2026-10-12 (low-risk, but will announce in #infra-alerts).
- Observations: Handoff template works well; reminder to include known noisy alerts in the ‘suppressions’ section to help new on-call engineers triage faster.

4) Postmortems and follow-ups
- KV cache degradation postmortem draft created (linked artifact CONFLUENCE-9876). Root cause analysis in draft, and timeline appended. No blameless issues raised; rollout process notes to be updated.
- Follow-ups: test harness and circuit-breaker tasks as above; backlog ticket created for adding canary traffic checks before cache tuning rollouts (owner: Maya Thompson, ticket: ENG-SRE-1453).

5) Changes deployed / Scheduled maintenance
- Deployed: small update to synthetic probe backoff and improved logging for eviction scheduler (rolled back the problematic config as part of incident mitigation).
- Scheduled: control-plane config push (non-disruptive) on 2026-10-12 02:00–03:00 PDT to roll in monitoring agent improvements. Will post a reminder in #eng-notifications and include a short maintenance window notice for partners who rely on strict SLA windows.

6) Capacity & Reliability work
- Autoscaling windows adjusted for embeddings workers in us-west-2 to reduce cold start latencies during known peak times. Monitoring will run for two weeks to validate efficacy.
- Investigating container CPU pinning for model-workers to reduce noisy neighbor effects (spike source shown in flame graphs collected during p99 events).

7) Actions / To-dos (owners and ETAs)
- Liam Chen: build eviction storm test harness and add synthetic traffic patterns (ETA: 2026-10-17).
- Noah Ramirez: design and implement eviction scheduler circuit-breaker and fallback path (ETA: 2026-10-24).
- Maya Thompson: create canary traffic check for cache-tuning rollouts; add to rollout checklist (ETA: 2026-10-20).
- Priya Desai: finalize postmortem and share with CS for customer notes (ETA: 2026-10-13).

8) Risks / Notes for leadership
- If embedding p99 latency remains elevated after autoscaling tweaks, we should consider temporarily routing heavy embedding workloads to a lower-latency dedicated pool to protect the hosted API SLOs. Cost implication analysis needed (owner: engineering leads).
- Staffing note: two SRE team members will be OOO 2026-10-18–22; plan on lighter on-call rotations that week.

9) Misc / shout-outs
- Shout-out to Priya and the on-call responders for rapid diagnosis and clean rollback during the eviction incident.
- Thanks to the observability team for fast access to flame graphs and eviction queue metrics.

10) Meeting notes / standups this week
- Daily standups covered: eviction work, embeddings latency investigation, synthetic probe fixes.
- Weekly SRE sync (2026-10-09): discussed rollout safety improvements and canary strategy; alignment with product for communication to Dedicated customers.

If anything needs to be added to the postmortem or action list, please reply in-thread or add directly to CONFLUENCE-9876.

-- Aisha
